entityDescription:
Dynas+ Group is an engineering company specialized in numerical simulation. Thanks to our long-standing partnerships with the major software publishers Ansys (https://www.ansys.com/) and DEP USA (https://depusa.com/), we distribute internationally recognized engineering software solutions such as LS-DYNA, Ansys Discovery, Ansys Mechanical, Fluent, HFSS, Maxwell and DEP MeshWorks. We support our industrial clients in Europe in optimizing their development cycles by providing tailored expertise services: technical support, training, subcontracting, consulting, methodology development, and R&D.
Our historical core expertise (over 30 years of experience) lies in the modeling and analysis of fast dynamics phenomena as well as the simulation of complex multi-physics phenomena using the LS-DYNA software. Over the years, this expertise has been strengthened by integrating complementary software, enabling our engineering office to expand its scope and address increasingly complex technical challenges in a wide range of industries such as aerospace, automotive, defense, marine, nuclear, and industrial goods.
Dynas+ places research and innovation at the heart of its strategy and actively participates in several collaborative innovation projects in the space, aeronautics and defense sectors. Every day, Dynas+ strives to create more efficient, faster, and more innovative solutions thanks to its committed collaborators and continuously enriched expertise.

Dynas+ has developed strong expertise in the simulation of hypervelocity impacts of orbital debris on space structures using LS-DYNA, supporting the analysis and design of resilient spacecraft components. This work has led to the filing of a patent related to an innovative structural concept specifically designed to improve resistance to debris impacts. In addition, Dynas+ has significant experience in the simulation of shock wave propagation resulting from pyrotechnic events within launcher and satellite structures.
In 2025, we are strengthening our European presence with the creation of Dynas+ Iberia, based in Madrid, to better support our new partners and clients in Spain and Portugal.

Baüne develops, manufactures, and deploys human‑centric autonomous care technologies that function from clinical settings to extreme and aerospace environments. This includes data‑processing platforms, real‑time analytics, medical‑grade systems integration, applied research, prototype development, and mission‑critical engineering for civilian, aerospace, and defense partners. The company maintains compliance pathways aligned with ISO 13485, MDSAP, and ISO 27701, ensuring readiness for regulated deployments across healthcare, performance, and mission‑driven sectors. 
Baüne’s structure remains intentionally lean and execution‑driven. Baüne Terrestrial Department focuses on medical‑technology deployment, system manufacturing, cybersecurity, and data‑platform development, supporting hospitals, clinics, and performance organizations. entityDescription: Suplac Rafinarie SRL este o societate cu răspundere limitată românească (CUI 46663303), înregistrată în România, stat membru ESA. Directorul companiei, Prof. Sergiu Vasili Lazarev (ORCID: 0009-0005-3749-9735), este cercetătorul principal și unicul coordonator științific al acestei propuneri.Prof. Lazarev desfășoară cercetări independente în fizica teoretică și computațională din 2010, cu aplicații directe în dinamica fluidelor, modelarea turbulenței și aerotermodinică. Peste 15 ani de cercetare au produs peste 50 de publicații evaluate de colegi și dezvoltarea cadrului New Subquantum Informational Mechanics (NMSI), din care a fost derivat solverul Navier-Stokes augmentat NSE-NMSI (NMSIFoam).Competența principală în dinamica fluidelor include: regularizarea analitică a ecuațiilor Navier-Stokes prin intermediul unor operatori matematici noi (DZO, gamma_diss, scalarea timpului fractal T_F); implementarea NMSIFoam ca modul de rezolvare OpenFOAM v2312; și validarea numerică a predicției turbulenței hipersonice la Mach 8-20 în raport cu datele de referință open-source NASA, atingând reduceri medii ale erorilor de 68% în comparație cu RANS k-omega SST standard (TRL-4 confirmat, 5 cazuri de referință).

entityDescription:
Spaceneedle helps high-value crop growers who struggle with weather-driven losses turn uncertainty into clear, profitable field action. In Poland and across the EU, droughts, frosts, and heatwaves are increasing while most operational decisions still rely on generic forecasts and delayed signals. Growers need plot-level clarity early enough to prevent damage, not just report it.
Our platform combines Copernicus satellite data (Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2) with Galileo-synchronized ground sensors to produce real-time microclimate intelligence and actionable recommendations. The result is a practical decision system for irrigation, fertigation, and frost response that can also automate selected workflows. We focus on both outcomes and usability: protect yield per hectare, reduce water waste, and simplify daily decision-making for farm teams.

entityDescription:
Baltic Space Systems Sp. z o.o. is a polish startup focused on the development of compact inertial navigation systems (INS) for unmanned platforms. Our devices are engineered to function in environments where satellite navigation signals are degraded or unavailable. They facilitate autonomous orientation and positioning without reliance on external information, thereby significantly enhancing resilience against GNSS jamming, spoofing, and interference during missions.
We originally developed the technology for rocket applications; however, due to its modular architecture, we have broadened our offerings to include two additional variants: satellite and drone.
A fundamental aspect of our approach is a unified device "core" the computational and algorithmic architecture, which we customize during production by selecting the type and quantity of sensors utilized in the system. This enables us to meticulously align the product with the customer's priorities, enhancing accuracy or optimizing cost.
In practice, this means we can provide various levels of precision without the need to redesign the entire system, merely by adjusting the sensor configuration within the same architecture.

They facilitate autonomous orientation and positioning without reliance on external information, thereby significantly enhancing resilience against GNSS jamming, spoofing, and interference during missions.
We originally developed the technology for rocket applications; however, due to its modular architecture, we have broadened our offerings to include two additional variants: satellite and drone.
A fundamental aspect of our approach is a unified device "core" the computational and algorithmic architecture, which we customize during production by selecting the type and quantity of sensors utilized in the system. This enables us to meticulously align the product with the customer's priorities, enhancing accuracy or optimizing cost.
In practice, this means we can provide various levels of precision without the need to redesign the entire system, merely by adjusting the sensor configuration within the same architecture.

entityDescription: TomoSAR France is a specialized service and consulting company in Earth Observation (EO), focusing on remote sensing and geomatics. The company leverages geospatial data from satellite (including Synthetic Aperture Radar - SAR) and airborne sensors to provide expert analysis, monitoring, and innovative solutions in France and internationally. Core activities include the detection, analysis, and tracking of infrastructure and terrain deformations using Interferometric SAR (InSAR) techniques, as well as the surveillance of vegetation, forest ecosystems (forestry), and agricultural resources. TomoSAR France designs, develops, and markets advanced software solutions based on the processing of multi-sensor imagery (Optical, Radar, LiDAR) at all spatial and temporal resolutions. This expertise extends to Big Data management, the production of Geographic Information Systems (GIS), and the development of webmapping solutions for urban and natural environment monitoring. Additionally, the company engages in commercial intermediation for professional geomatics training, connecting training organizations with clients and providing consulting, business development, and marketing services. The corporate object also includes strategic operations such as the creation of new companies, the acquisition of patents, and the participation in mergers or alliances to foster its growth and development. The company combines multi-orbit satellite data, artificial intelligence, IoT ground sensors, and insurance analytics to predict, prevent, and mitigate environmental and climate-related risks.

Prometheus supports European and global climate-resilience objectives, including alignment with UN SDG 13 and the EU Green Deal Resilience Framework, aiming to transition risk management from reactive compensation to predictive prevention.

entityDescription:
What is 'PwC'?
PwC is the brand under which the member firms of PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited (PwCIL) operate and provide professional services. Together, these firms form the PwC network. ‘PwC’ is often used to refer either to individual firms within the PwC network or to several or all of them collectively.
In many parts of the world, accounting firms are required by law to be locally owned and independent. Although regulatory attitudes on this issue are changing, PwC member firms do not and cannot currently operate as a corporate multinational. The PwC network is not a global partnership, a single firm, or a multinational corporation.
For these reasons, the PwC network consists of firms which are separate legal entities. The firms that make up the network are committed to working together to provide quality service offerings for clients throughout the world. Firms in the PwC network are members in, or have other connections to, PricewaterhouseCoopers International Limited (PwCIL), an English private company limited by guarantee. PwCIL does not practise accountancy or provide services to clients. Rather its purpose is tofacilitate coordination betweenmember firms in the PwC network. Focusing on key areas such as strategy, brand, and risk and quality, the Network Leadership Team and Board of PwCIL develop and implement policies and initiatives to achieve a common and coordinated approach among individual firms where appropriate. Member firms of PwCIL can use the PwC name and the resources and methodologies of the PwC network are made available to them. In addition, member firms may request the resources of other member firms and/or secure the provision of professional services by other member firms and/or other entities. In return, member firms agree to abide by certain common policies and to maintain the standards of the PwC network as put forward by PwCIL.
The PwC network is not one international partnership and PwC member firms are not otherwise legal partners with each other. Many of the member firms have legally registered names which contain “PricewaterhouseCoopers”, however there is no ownership by PwCIL. A member firm cannot act as agent of PwCIL or any other member firm, cannot obligate PwCIL or any other member firm, and is liable only for its own acts or omissions and not those of PwCIL or any other member firm. Similarly, PwCIL cannot act as an agent of any member firm, cannot obligate any member firm, and is liable only for its own acts or omissions.

entityDescription:
MatAlytics Ltd is a UK based deep technology company developing advanced AI solutions for real time structural integrity and asset life assessment in heavy industry.
Founded as a spin out from the University of Nottingham, MatAlytics combines high fidelity finite element engineering models with physics informed artificial intelligence to create its core platform, CITRUS Component Integrity Technology Reliability Utilisation System. The technology enables near instantaneous prediction of stresses, fatigue, creep damage, and remaining useful life of critical components such as pressure vessels, steam drums, piping systems, and high temperature structures.
Unlike conventional methods that rely on periodic offline simulations or conservative rule based approaches, MatAlytics bridges design and operation by translating live plant data into physically interpretable engineering metrics in real time. This allows operators to make safer, faster, and more economically optimised decisions, particularly for assets operating under flexible duty cycles or beyond original design life.
The company serves power generation, nuclear, oil and gas, and other safety critical industrial sectors, working closely with major utilities and industrial partners to deploy physics based AI within existing analytics environments.
MatAlytics’ mission is to redefine how engineering decisions are made, moving from static assessment to continuous physics grounded intelligence.

Founded as a spin out from the University of Nottingham, MatAlytics combines high fidelity finite element engineering models with physics informed artificial intelligence to create its core platform, CITRUS Component Integrity Technology Reliability Utilisation System. The technology enables near instantaneous prediction of stresses, fatigue, creep damage, and remaining useful life of critical components such as pressure vessels, steam drums, piping systems, and high temperature structures.
Unlike conventional methods that rely on periodic offline simulations or conservative rule based approaches, MatAlytics bridges design and operation by translating live plant data into physically interpretable engineering metrics in real time. This allows operators to make safer, faster, and more economically optimised decisions, particularly for assets operating under flexible duty cycles or beyond original design life.
The company serves power generation, nuclear, oil and gas, and other safety critical industrial sectors, working closely with major utilities and industrial partners to deploy physics based AI within existing analytics environments.
MatAlytics’ mission is to redefine how engineering decisions are made, moving from static assessment to continuous physics grounded intelligence.

entityDescription:
Addyx is an innovative Italian startup founded in 2021, specializing in the development of proprietary technologies for advanced composite manufacturing. The company focuses on enabling the efficient production of high-performance hollow structures with complex geometries, addressing key limitations of traditional manufacturing systems.
Addyx operates primarily in the aerospace, automotive, marine, and high-performance sports industries — sectors where lightweight design, structural efficiency, and manufacturing repeatability are essential competitive drivers.
The company’s core strength lies in its patented technologies designed to improve the production of hollow composite components.
WSM-170 is an expandable, water-soluble mandrel engineered for manufacturing hollow tubular composite parts. It simplifies the layup process, improves internal surface quality, reduces waste, and allows easier removal after curing, increasing overall process efficiency.
Carbon Exoskeleton is a system of topologically optimized structural reinforcements integrated into composite components. It enhances stiffness and mechanical performance while minimizing weight, enabling more efficient structural designs.
RM-X is a next-generation reinforced sacrificial mandrel technology developed for producing hollow composite structures with complex geometries, including undercuts, nodes, and variable cross-sections. The system consists of a thin external shell made from water-soluble polymer combined with an internal structural reinforcement core, also fully water-soluble. This configuration ensures mechanical stability during curing while allowing complete dissolution in water after processing. The result is reduced material usage, lower production times, improved repeatability, and cost efficiency.
Addyx integrates advanced CAD design, structural simulation, additive manufacturing, rotomolding, and hybrid manufacturing techniques. The company develops functional prototypes, industrial demonstrators, and proof-of-concept projects in collaboration with industrial partners, supporting OEMs and Tier 1 suppliers in optimizing their composite manufacturing processes.
Its business model combines direct supply of devices and engineered solutions with a scalable approach that includes technology licensing. By leveraging strong intellectual property protection and process know-how, Addyx positions itself as a technology partner for companies seeking to manufacture lighter, stronger, and more sustainable composite structures.
The company’s vision is to become a reference player in advanced composite manufacturing technologies, transforming geometric complexity into a competitive advantage and enabling new structural architectures that can be reliably industrialized at scale.
